# ANALYSIS: BULLISH_RECLAIM_EXIT_STYLE_COMPARISON

**Filed:** 2026-08-01
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** exit_style_analysis
**Status:** DRAFT

## Hypothesis

Splitting entries (TP1 + trail) for BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setups will yield higher profitability and better risk-adjusted returns compared to all-or-nothing exits because it allows capturing partial gains on quick reversals while letting runners extend on strong trends, aligning with the setup's inherent asymmetry.

## Method

We will conduct a Stage-1 backtest using the BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup rules as defined in the playbook, comparing two exit variants:
- Variant A (current): TP1 at +50% premium (selling 2/3 of position), then trailing the remaining 1/3 via chandelier profit-lock (arms at +5%, trails 0.15) until runner exit signals (close into ribbon, rejection signature, or 3x premium).
- Variant B (all-or-nothing): Exit entire position at the first of: TP1 at +50% premium, or stop-out at chart-stop (rejected level + $0.50 buffer) or premium stop (-50% for Safe, -5% bull for Bold) or time stop (15:50 ET).

We will use the same entry triggers and position sizing (3 contracts minimum) for both variants. We will run the backtest on the available 16-month SPY 5m data (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) using real OPRA fills simulator.

## Confidence

3 / 10 -- We have no data to support the hypothesis at this time. The playbook's current exit style (TP1 + trail) is based on the bearish version which has shown promise, but the bullish version is untested. We need to run the backtest to see if the bullish setup exhibits similar asymmetry.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This analysis does not directly conflict with any existing candidate. It may inform a future candidate proposal for adjusting the exit style of the BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup.
